ConnectionStrings.//NOTE: Default LocalDB connection for local development in Visual Studio (02-SYSTEM-ARCHITECTURE.md / 03-DATABASE-SCHEMA.md: SQL Server via EF Core Code-First). Point this at a different SQL Server instance for a real deployment, with a least-privilege login (db_datareader + db_datawriter only - see security-test-report.md F4) and Encrypt=True;TrustServerCertificate=False once there's a real certificate.

Jwt.//NOTE: security-test-report.md F1: this file no longer ships a real signing key (an earlier version committed one directly - treat that value as burned if it was ever deployed anywhere, and rotate it). Set a real key OUTSIDE this file before running in anything but Development: `dotnet user-secrets set "Jwt:Key" "$(openssl rand -base64 48)"` locally, or a Jwt__Key environment variable on a real server. In Development only, Program.cs generates a random key automatically when this is left blank, purely so `dotnet run` still works with zero setup right after a clone.
Jwt.//NOTE-ExpiryHours: Tightened from 8 to 2 (security-test-report.md F11) - long enough for most of a shift without re-login, short enough that a leaked token stops being useful reasonably quickly. Raise it back if that trade-off is wrong for how your staff actually work, or move to short-lived tokens + refresh tokens later for a stronger version of the same idea.

//NOTE-FrontendBaseUrl: Used only to build the link encoded inside each table's QR code (06-QR-CODE-AND-TABLE-FLOW.md). Update this to the real public URL when deployed; https://localhost:7052 matches Option A (this project serving the frontend from wwwroot/) from 02-SYSTEM-ARCHITECTURE.md.
//NOTE-Cors: Only read outside Development (see Program.cs) - Option A (frontend served from this app's own wwwroot/) never needs this at all, since that's always same-origin. Only fill this in for Option B (frontend hosted separately), with the real deployed frontend origin(s), e.g. ["https://menu.your-restaurant.com"]. security-test-report.md F9.
//NOTE-SeedDemoAccounts: security-test-report.md F5: defaults to false now - a previous version defaulted to true, which meant a fresh deployment created a real admin/kitchen account with a well-known password unless someone remembered to turn this off. Set it to true yourself for local testing (see README.md) if you want the seeded admin/kitchen accounts; SeedData.cs's own default is also false as a second safety net in case this key is ever removed from the file entirely.
